# Experimental Apple decoder

Remora's explicit `apple` VNC mode implements one plaintext Apple RFB 003.889 profile. Standard mode remains the default. Apple mode requires security type 30 (ARD), an extended shared ServerInit without session selection, 32-bit RGB888 pixels, and an initial complete framebuffer baseline. It advertises only MVS encoding 1011 and Raw. Unsupported profiles and geometry changes end the attempt. There is no alternate authentication retry, whole-session encryption, virtual display, media, HEVC, clipboard synchronization or dynamic resizing. The only reconnection is the same-profile transport recovery described under Connection reliability.

`mvs.c` and `mvs.h` are the frozen v3 C port of [noVNC-ARD](https://github.com/peetinc/noVNC-ARD/tree/d699293635083c9e0c30c8f9480993865653772a/ard/decoders), revision `d699293635083c9e0c30c8f9480993865653772a`. The port covers full, partial, cache, match and quantization updates. The imported algorithm is unchanged. Only the historical scratch description and header guard were changed for this distribution. The originals had SHA-256 `7efd6151967b4bb1313f8f849cbd284663a5554542c8e459e144d0a470cd87fd` (C) and `2da0cf4349d12f2ed8289e399a230c011a7b609ed7299d3bec33f7c4e6f08c45` (header). The MPL-2.0 license is in `../licenses/Apple-MVS-MPL-2.0.txt`. The IDCT attribution and IJG notices are retained. New adapter code is GPL-3.0-or-later.

The reference JavaScript wraps IDCT intermediate arithmetic to 32 bits. This C port computes the transform in 64 bits with the documented 32-bit workspace. Independent valid-stream comparisons found differences when dequantized coefficient magnitudes reached 32768 or greater. Apple's behavior in that range is unverified. Partial-state accumulation prevents assuming that real content cannot reach it. No overflow emulation or decoder change is made here. Cache slots 1 through 64999 are supported and wrap to 1. Index 65000 always ends the session with a typed error, including cache-next after 64999. The JavaScript reference accepts this unwritten slot after 65000 inserts and reads past its typed array. Remora does not reproduce that behavior; Apple encoder/viewer behavior at that index is unknown. Full agreement with Apple's decoder remains unproven. Real-host validation is limited to the LAN measurements and editing workload below. The controlled Apple-viewer oracle covered only F0 and F1; its rejected F2 image was deleted and F3-F6 were not evaluated.

`apple.c` owns the private profile state. It parses bounded control bodies, limits compressed rectangles to the smaller of 64 MiB and `4 * rectangle area + 65536`, and accepts only aligned, framebuffer-contained MVS rectangles. The existing renderer limits remain 16384 pixels per axis and 67,108,864 pixels total. A malformed rectangle ends the session. There is no recovery using a partially consumed payload or a decoder that has failed.

Whole updates commit only after all rectangles validate. The adapter accumulates one bounding box from the decoder's existing written-tile callbacks and Raw rectangles, then publishes it once at the end of the message. DCT writes, cache loads and match copies contribute only their destination pixels, clipped at the framebuffer edge. Skipped tiles, skipped matches and quantization updates add no damage. A full MVS update publishes the entire desktop. The first complete baseline also publishes the entire desktop; unsupported geometry changes still end the attempt. One bounding box uses constant storage and preserves the existing single-rectangle renderer path. Distant writes can include unchanged pixels between them. No callback exposes an incomplete message, even if the decoder wrote pixels before detecting its error.

The adapter sends shared ClientInit `0x81` and control SetMode 1 before the initial full FramebufferUpdateRequest. It then enables full-region, zero-interval AutoFBUpdate (`0x09`) before waiting for a baseline. While visible and awaiting a complete baseline, the worker retries a full, non-incremental request once per second between messages. Controls and incomplete coverage do not reset that retry interval. Partial MVS frames still require a complete baseline. It sends no automatic type-3 request per pushed update. Hidden demand pauses retries and sends AutoFBUpdate interval `0xffffffff`; resume sends interval 0 and preserves the existing immediate full-refresh request. Both subscription messages use header flags 1. Repeated demand does not generate refreshes. Closing the transport ends the subscription.

These startup and pause records follow the arm64e ScreenSharing framework and AppleVNCServer installed with macOS 27.0.1 (26A434). ScreenSharing's `stRequestUpdates` sends `RFBCheckForUpdate(ref, 1, NULL)` at `0x1cc068044`, then calls `stSetFrameUpdateInterval` at `0x1cc068214` before receiving a frame. `stSetFrameUpdateInterval` passes AutoFBUpdate flags 1 and maps a negative interval to `0xffffffff` at `0x1cc0daf18`. AppleVNCServer's `HandleAutoFrameBufferUpdateMessage` at `0x10001708c` enables automatic updates exactly when the interval differs from `0xffffffff`. SetMode 0 observes, SetMode 1 controls, and SetMode 2 inhibits local physical input when the server permits it. SetMode does not select a frame rate; Remora uses SetMode 1.

Server messages ARDAck (`0x04`), NOP (`0x07`), StateChange (`0x14`) and DisplayInfo2 (`0x51`) are handled only in this profile. Basic and Apple pasteboard bodies are discarded in chunks of at most 4096 bytes, with a 1 MiB body limit. Unknown messages and unsupported rectangle encodings fail closed.

Key and pointer events use the source-defined combined type `0x10`, flag 0 and a 16-byte AES-128-ECB block. Key-only blocks contain marker 255, direction and BE32 keysym in bytes 0 through 5. Pointer-only blocks contain marker 255, the button mask and BE16 coordinates in bytes 10 through 15. The unused half stays zero. Both kinds share the elapsed monotonic microseconds in bytes 6 through 9, modulo 2^32. The previous timestamp starts at zero, matching Screen Sharing, so the first event carries the low 32 bits of uptime. Flag 0 leaves the click count unspecified. This is Screen Sharing's 18-byte fallback; it requires no shared timebase. Only the ARD-derived 16-byte MD5 shared-secret key is retained after successful authentication. OpenSSL performs AES. Native state, key and block buffers are cleansed on failure, reinitialization and worker cleanup. No key enters Swift or diagnostics. The desktop transport remains unencrypted. The normal security selector still prefers VeNCrypt, but this Apple profile ends if the selected method is not ARD because no supported event key exists.

Option maps to Meta, legacy character keysyms above Latin-1 map to Unicode, and right/middle button bits swap at the Apple wire boundary. Source ownership stays in the existing input worker. Discrete scrolling follows ard-rs revision `7ff47199541c364cbba16e29c4410e39898ece0e`, `crates/ard-core/src/protocol.rs:917` and `crates/ard-viewer/src/session_runtime.rs:2058`. Positive native horizontal deltas correspond to RFB left (0x20); Remora right (0x40) becomes negative. Discrete scrolling uses the source-defined type `0x17`, subtype 11 record with line, 16.16 and point deltas, the event position, and the existing held-button mask. A local system arrow is explicitly emitted; unsupported remote cursor-shape encodings are not advertised.

`../patches/libvncclient-apple.patch` connects this module to the pinned LibVNCClient without changing standard-mode parsing or authentication selection. `../build-vnc.sh` compiles this decoder in the Release engine with `-O3`, using the existing OpenSSL archive. `../tests/test-apple-mvs.sh` runs the owned vectors and bounded fuzz cases under ASan/UBSan. `python3 Vendor/tests/test-apple-session.py` drives the sanitized adapter and decoder through the public native API with an independently authenticated loopback peer. Swift public-session tests exercise the same wire framing and independent CommonCrypto key-event decryption. None of these tests establish Apple-viewer fidelity or real-host usability.

## Responsiveness on LAN

On 2026-11-12 a development build on a MacBook Pro M4 Pro running macOS 27.0.1 was compared with Screen Sharing's standard connection, using Adaptive Quality, against a MacBook Pro M3 Pro running macOS 26.6.2 on the same LAN. Each client displayed the same 3024x1964 desktop in a 1512x1034 window. A local probe posted physical input and timed the first changed pixels in the client window with ScreenCaptureKit. It requested 120 Hz capture on a 60 Hz display; this measures captured response, not physical display latency.

Six alternating Apple-mode/Screen Sharing pairs ran one client at a time, with 16 trials per action in each round. Scroll alternated six lines down and up. Typing alternated one physical A key and Delete, with the pointer outside the text region. Each insertion shifted the watched line by one cell, and each deletion restored it exactly. Menu trials alternated opening TextEdit's File menu and closing it with Escape. Every trial in these six pairs observed a response. Standard mode ran one further round with the same physical inputs, window geometry and thresholds.

Each cell is the median of the per-round medians in milliseconds. Parentheses give the population standard deviation of those round medians. Typing and menu columns measure insertion and opening; scroll includes both directions.

| Client | Scroll | Type | Open menu | Rounds |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Remora Apple mode | 75 (7.0) | 66 (8.8) | 122 (9.5) | 6 |
| macOS Screen Sharing | 72 (4.3) | 66 (9.6) | 115 (7.2) | 6 |
| Remora standard mode | 621 | 396 | 1145 | 1 |

Apple mode's three median gaps are below 10 ms, and it is faster than standard mode for every action. The variance criterion in #68 is still unmet: Apple mode's scroll and menu round medians vary more than Screen Sharing's. Typing variance is lower. Deletion medians are 63 ms for Apple mode and 71 ms for Screen Sharing; menu closing medians are 155 ms and 148 ms. Standard mode takes 397 ms for deletion and 233 ms for menu closing. Its scroll round trips did not restore the watched region exactly, so the scroll comparison establishes response to the same input rather than equal final scroll distance.

Per-round medians below are Apple mode / Screen Sharing, in milliseconds.

| Round | Scroll | Type | Open menu |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 78.0 / 68.2 | 58.9 / 76.2 | 120.7 / 104.5 |
| 2 | 73.4 / 77.1 | 80.9 / 90.9 | 132.3 / 113.3 |
| 3 | 85.9 / 76.9 | 69.1 / 64.3 | 141.5 / 121.6 |
| 4 | 75.7 / 70.0 | 71.5 / 64.7 | 115.9 / 117.6 |
| 5 | 65.6 / 73.1 | 54.6 / 67.3 | 114.9 / 113.2 |
| 6 | 66.0 / 65.6 | 61.9 / 65.4 | 122.4 / 127.4 |

Rounds 1-3 used `7ee3d82`; rounds 4-6 used `a9a3584`, which adds startup recovery without changing steady-state input or rendering. A separate A-B-B-A experiment with 16 menu trials per block tested a non-incremental full request after input. It improved opening by about 10 ms but slowed closing by about 19 ms and forced additional full-desktop work, so it was removed. Accepted timing runs used neither tracing nor concurrent captures. Calibration failures and pre-input capture/geometry failures are retained separately. One earlier menu-close probe timed out although the next capture showed the menu closed; its cause remains unproven. Raw trials, metadata, the frozen probe and the summary calculation are under `.snap/benchmark/final/`.

The decoder and image-quality settings are unchanged. A 303-second editing workload is described below. In the earlier 2026-11-08 comparison, Escape in Preview's empty search field left the focus ring visible in both Remora and Screen Sharing; that behavior came from Preview.

## Connection reliability

On 2026-11-12 a signed development build on macOS 27.0.1 connected to a MacBook Pro M3 Pro running macOS 26.6.2 over LAN. A final run on `a9a3584` completed 100 consecutive Apple-mode connections, each returning a nonblack 3024x1964 picture. Every attempt saved a PNG, independently decoded its pixels and recorded its SHA-256 before closing the session. This run needed no recovery handshake. An earlier build also passed 100 consecutive connections, plus three connections that each followed 180 seconds with no VNC client connected. The host used its existing display policy on AC power. Final receipts and images are under `.snap/benchmark/connects-recovery/`; earlier evidence is under `.snap/benchmark/connects-final/` and `.snap/benchmark/connects-idle/`.

Before the recovery fix, one of 112 authenticated connections to the same host received no ServerInit. The host was awake and unlocked. Remora's summary read `native_error=6 phase=18 last_success=17 failure=10`: ARD authentication succeeded and ClientInit was written, but no ServerInit byte arrived before the 10-second read deadline. The host's log and `screensharingd` disassembly identify a lost wakeup in macOS 26.6.2 (25G83). Its authentication thread wakes the server loop before adding the authenticated socket to the descriptor set. The loop can then wait indefinitely without that socket. In the failed connection the log order was reversed from all 111 successful connections, and the server read the waiting ClientInit only when another client connected 224.7 seconds later. macOS 27.0.1 (26A434) adds the socket before sending the wakeup. Nine other first connections to newly started daemons succeeded, so daemon startup or idle time alone does not explain the stall. Logs, analysis and disassembly extracts are under `.snap/serverinit-timeout/`.

Remora recovers from exactly this state once per session. When the Apple profile has selected ARD, the server has accepted authentication, ClientInit has been written, and the ServerInit read reaches its deadline without receiving a byte, the bridge reports error 11. The session worker then frees that native context, with its socket, decoder state and ARD key. It opens one new context to the same endpoint with the same profile and the same credentials. A password typed for the first transport is reused for the second and then dropped. Rejected authentication, cancellation, EOF, a partial ServerInit and standard mode are never retried, and no other security type is tried. The existing 20-second connection deadline covers both transports. Each transport writes its own handshake summary under the same attempt UUID, and the first keeps `native_error=11` with its phase and failure numbers. `appleWithheldServerInitRecoversOnceOnAFreshTransport` covers the recovery against the independent loopback peer. The stall cannot be forced on a real host. The one real-host observation is the manual reconnect 224.7 seconds later, which succeeded while the stalled viewer was still registered.

A 303-second TextEdit workload completed 100 paired typing/deleting, scrolling and File-menu cycles with live frames throughout. Periodic PNGs and independently decoded movie frames showed no visible decoding errors. A static first-line region matched the initial capture exactly after the workload, and the generated document's saved bytes were unchanged. Evidence is under `.snap/apple-editing/run-20261112T133657Z-db7fdf/`.
